records.supported_name_scope: Río Salado is supported as the representative system identity. The selected modeled mainstem approaches through a southern feeder, Brandsen and Las Flores before joining the lower Salado; it is not entirely a river named Salado. The grouped upper Salado and other branches retain their own identities and model relationships.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Correspondence uses the complete three-piece selected route: northwestern headwater approach, northeastward Blanca Grande–General Alvear corridor, eastward and northward confluence approach, then the lower Salado's southward bend and northeastward coastal exit. Buenos Aires is an editorial qualifier distinguishing other Salado rivers.
records.region: Central Buenos Aires Province, Argentina, from the Olavarría–Blanca Grande and Las Flores approach to the lower Salado and Bahía Samborombón; grouped branches extend northwest through Junín and west into the Vallimanca lowlands.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence for all three selected modeled-mainstem pieces and the nine-piece group context. Exact feeder names, naming-transition vertices, artificial-versus-natural reach boundaries and modern channel positions are not assigned.

naming_scope_details.geographic_qualifier: Buenos Aires, Argentina; editorial disambiguation only.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Southern feeder–Brandsen–Las Flores approach retained separately; the modeled mainstem does not follow the named Salado's northwestern headwaters.
naming_scope_details.lake_wetland_scope: Blanca Grande, the Las Flores confluence wetlands and Junín-area lakes remain distinct water bodies and contexts.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Vallimanca, Saladillo, Las Flores and southern tributary contexts are not aliases. Grouped upper Salado retains its named identity despite its model role.
naming_scope_details.artificial_channel_scope: Canal 16 and other drainage works are distinct from natural streams. No exhaustive channel attribution is made for modeled links; Canal 15 is separate from the selected terminal Salado route.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Salado outlet into Bahía Samborombón; no exact river–estuary boundary assigned.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Connectivity, mainstem role and rendered length do not establish a single hydronym, perennial natural flow, surveyed source or modern engineered-channel alignment.

records.supported_name_scope: No natural river identity is established for the complete modeled Inland Ice path. This completed feature-class and naming-scope hold does not claim that every nearby marginal stream is unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: West-central Greenland Inland Ice around 66–68°N, with a western approach toward the ice margin north/northeast of the locality printed Søndre Strømfjord on the historical map. That locality and its fjord are context, not river-name assignments.
records.completion_scope: Readable coverage supports the completed scope hold. Positive natural-river identity evidence would be required before any later name assignment; no further acquisition is pending now.

naming_scope_details.length_limit: Model display length, not a measured natural-river length.

records.supported_name_scope: Petit Mécatina is supported as the representative drainage identity of this four-piece selection. The modeled trunk includes a western upper approach, Fourmont and other lake passages, the downstream Petit Mécatina corridor, and the separately named Nétagamiou outlet. The terminal is not the eastern Petit Mécatina mouth. The northeast tributary, initial feeder and exact lake or river-name transition vertices are not assigned uniform names.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual western southeast approach, repeated eastward bends, southeast descent, Fourmont continuation, long southward course and southern coastal outlet were compared with readable original provincial cartography and an original delta aerial mosaic. The regional upper-route comparison is representative-scale, not vertex-level or a surveyed headwater identification.
records.region: Eastern Québec and southern Labrador, Canada, from the western upper lake country through the Fourmont corridor to the Basse-Côte-Nord and Gulf of St. Lawrence.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence for all four selected fragments. The acquired regional and eastern PATP sheets, delta map and direct station descriptions suffice. No further source is required for this finding; the already-started optional Portrait territorial download is outside the evidential basis. Exact feeder, tributary and transition naming would be separate work.

naming_scope_details.english_corridor_form: Little Mecatina River is directly used by Newfoundland and Labrador for the upper corridor above Fourmont; no formal bilingual naming decision is asserted.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Western feeder and lake-chain correspondence is established at regional-map scale only. The precise named-river source, every small connection and the exact start of the Petit Mécatina hydronym remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Fourmont and other intervening waterbody passages remain lakes, not blanket river-name equivalents. No lake assessment is reopened and no exact entry or exit vertex is assigned.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Fragment 9315 is a separate northeast tributary. A local tributary name is not assigned from a nearby label, a station point or MAIN_RIV membership.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: The modeled ending follows Rivière Nétagamiou. The eastern Petit Mécatina coastal branch is separate from the selected ending. Exact split vertex, estuary-channel details and contemporary shoreline are not fixed.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Modeled mainstem roles and display lengths are not natural-river length, current discharge or surveyed naming boundaries. Historical map border annotations are not adopted as a determination of the Québec–Labrador boundary. No naming date, Indigenous-name equivalence or current legal fishing advice is established.

records.supported_name_scope: Horton River is supported as the representative identity of this selected upper-to-coastal corridor. The headward model endpoint is not a surveyed source, Horton Lake remains a separate adjoining waterbody, and the terminal coastal extension is not assigned an exact modern mouth or abandoned-channel name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The complete selected path was compared with the readable original GNWT ecological map and its regional descriptions. Its east-to-west upper approach, northwestward upland passage, westward lower-middle elbow and northward coastal reach distinguish it from the Anderson drainage to the west and Hornaday drainage to the east. Northwest Territories is an editorial qualifier.
records.region: Arctic mainland Northwest Territories, Canada, from the upper corridor north and east of Horton Lake through the Horton uplands and Smoking Hills to the Franklin Bay setting.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence for the one selected fragment. The acquired official map, direct regional text and terminal imagery suffice. Exact headwater and feeder names, naming-transition vertices and present delta channels are outside the completed finding; no further acquisition is pending.

naming_scope_details.geographic_qualifier: Northwest Territories, Canada; editorial disambiguation only.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Eastern model endpoint and individual feeder names remain unassigned; no surveyed source or complete named headwaters claimed.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Horton Lake is separate adjoining lake context south of the selected upper river, not a river alias or an implied lake traversal.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: West River, Coal Creek and other feeders remain separate. Anderson and Hornaday are distinct neighboring drainages.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Franklin Bay delta context is supported. No exact shoreline, modern outlet vertex, abandoned-channel name or historical diversion date is assigned.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Modeled mainstem role and display length do not establish a uniform official hydronym, natural-river length or contemporary channel geometry. No gazetteer naming decision or naming date was verified.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
